text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty: PD-8753 triggered — service=frontend high-error-rate-production. link: https://pd/redwood/PD-8753

Sam H: I'm on it, taking first responder. seeing 5xx spike on service/frontend across us-east-1.

Maria L: thanks Sam. any customer-facing impact yet?

Sam H: brief blip, 502s for a subset of requests to /api/generate. Error rate peaked ~18% for 10m, now ~6% after retry tuning. Can't say no customer impact — some sessions got errors.

Jen K: tagging @oncall-handoff so next team knows. recommend we triage alert noise after this. this thread for live mitigation + follow-up tuning.

Dave R: quick ask — do we have grouping on this PD? looks noisy; multiple hosts firing same alert.

Sam H: PD had 24 separate triggers (one per host). I silenced noisy hosts via PD UI but that's manual.

Maria L: dek. We should avoid manual silences for next time. propose: 1) add dedupe/grouping in monitoring rule 2) set rate-limit on PD route 3) create a compact troubleshooting dashboard.

Jen K: agreed. proposal details?

Sam H: My idea: route alerts by service+region and group by "alert fingerprint" (hash of query path + error class). Also add a per-route throttle (token bucket) at PD of 5 alerts/min for this route. Start conservative so we don't hide a major outage.

Dave R: 👍 on grouping. For dedupe: in Datadog we can use `aggregations` + `group by` on `host` vs `route`. Right now we group by host which creates N alerts. switch to group by `status_code`+`path_template`+`service`.

ops-bot: FYI: current alert rule definition (truncated):
```yaml
- name: frontend_high_error_rate
  query: "sum(last_1m):sum:requests.error{service:frontend}.as_count() / sum:requests.total{service:frontend}.as_count() > 0.1"
  group_by: ["host"]
  notify: pagerduty
```

Maria L: if we change `group_by` to ["service","path_template","status_category"] we get one alert per failing endpoint, not per host. That's better for incident triage.

Sam H: also propose we add a short dedupe window — coalesce identical alerts for 3m. That prevents immediate fanout during short spikes.

Jen K: what about suppressing known noisy sources? e.g., canaries emit some 5xx during deploys — route those to a lower-priority PD schedule or separate escalation.

Dave R: yep, add `exclude: env:canary` in the query and add a `tags`-based route for `deploy-canary` to a different PD schedule.

Maria L: on the PD side, we can add a filter in the routing rule that enforces a rate limit: `max_per_minute: 5` and `group_by: fingerprint`. That should cut down duplicate pages.

Sam H: plan for immediate mitigation (next 60m):
- 1) change PD route to 5/min throttle (ops engineer)
- 2) adjust monitoring rule group_by to service+path_template (SRE)
- 3) create small dashboard tile with 502s by path + host (observability)
- 4) document follow-up ticket for full dedupe implementation (alerts team)

Jen K: assigning owners: Dave -> PD route change, Maria -> monitoring rule, Jen -> dashboard, Sam -> follow-up ticket + customer impact notes.

Dave R: I'll flip PD throttle now. committing to 48h window. If we see hidden signal loss we rollback.

ops-bot: ACTION LOG: Dave R set PD route throttle for route `frontend-high-error-rate` to `5/min` at 1765003600.

Sam H: Maria — can you post the proposed alert snippet you want in Datadog?

Maria L: yes, here's a draft to swap in (tested in staging):
```yaml
query: "sum(last_1m):sum:requests.error{service:frontend,env:prod}.as_count() / sum:requests.total{service:frontend,env:prod}.as_count() > 0.1"
group_by: ["service","path_template","status_category"]
dedupe_window: 180 # seconds
notify: pagerduty
```

Jen K: that `dedupe_window` plus grouping should drastically reduce per-host fanout. nice.

Sam H: Jen — please build the dashboard with these two panels: 1) 502 rate by path (top 10) 2) 502 count heatmap by host vs path. quick filter for `trace_id` when investigating.

Jen K: on it. will push a dashboard draft to `#monitoring-dashboards` and link here.

Dave R: PD throttle live. monitoring will determine if we suppressed anything important. keep an eye on error percent vs user-visible errors.

ops-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: error-rate back to 2.4% — below alert threshold. PD alerts suppressed: 18 duplicates in the window.

Sam H: customers: no broad outage but some sessions failed. I filed a short incident summary for CS that they can use for customer comms. ticket: INC-4921.

Maria L: follow-ups (to capture in the post-incident ticket):
- implement alert grouping change in prod rule (owner: Maria)
- add dedupe_window parameter across high-card alerts (owner: alerts team)
- automate PD rate-limiting for noisy routes (owner: infra)
- dashboard (owner: Jen)
- review canary exclusion logic (owner: Sam)

Jen K: timeline estimate: grouping + dedupe in prod by EOD tomorrow if no blockers. dashboard within 24h. PD automation ticket to infra for next sprint.

Sam H: handoff: I'm handing to oncall-next (Maria) at 1765004120. leaving notes in INC-4921.

Maria L: thanks Sam. tagging this thread `postmortem-needed` and will create a short writeup with the tuning plan.

Dave R: small note — when we coalesce, ensure the alert still contains example event samples (host list) so we know where it happened. don't remove context.

Maria L: good call. add `top_hosts` traceback to the alert body.

Sam H: closing out live mitigation. big win: lower noise, maintain signal. we should monitor for missed signals over next 72h. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: This thread has been archived to the incident log. summary ticket: INC-4921.
